cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 24th District since 2017. Earlier worked on the staff of Santa Barbara County Supervisor Naomi Schwartz (1993–2004), then served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors (2004–2016). U.S. Marine Corps Reserve veteran. Holds degrees from UC Santa Barbara and Fielding Graduate University.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position or action from Carbajal on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, police pay and pensions, school choice or teacher pay. His campaign site lists "Pushing for Sensible Gun Laws" as an issue heading, but the page text we could read gave no specific position or action on red-flag laws or other gun measures. We could not read his full Ballotpedia key-vote list for earlier Congresses, because the page was cut off partway through the 117th Congress. We found no controversies about him in the pages we had.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: Santa Barbara County supervisor for 12 years (2004–2016) after 11 years on a supervisor's staff, then U.S. House member since 2017 with seats on the Agriculture, Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.
qual.why: Prior local executive-legislative office and nearly a decade as a member of Congress, plus long county staff experience, fit the lawmaking, oversight and constituent-service job.
qual.label: Prior local executive-legislative office and nearly a decade as a member of Congress, plus long county staff experience, fit the lawmaking, oversight and constituent-service job.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), which required DHS to detain certain undocumented immigrants arrested for theft-related offenses; the bill passed the House 263-156.

pro-life.evidence: He opposed the 2022 overturning of Roe v. Wade, calling it a "betrayal to our Constitution [and] a betrayal of millions of women who count on its protections to retain control of their own body and choices."

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says that as a county supervisor he stood up against developments on the Gaviota Coast that threatened preservation efforts, and that he is a leader in protecting scenic views and open spaces.
